subject: Proposal: Transitioning Velox AI to Annual Commit with Staggered Credits
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@velox.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-25T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot results + proposal to move to annual prepay

Hi Susan —

Great to hear the pilot latency and cost numbers are holding up on your side. As discussed on the call, moving to an annual prepay will give Velox better unit economics and predictable capacity during your ramp. I ran the numbers with finance and attached a draft proposal that preserves your production throughput while applying a staged credit schedule during the first 12 months.

High-level:
- 12-month annual commit (USD 360k) with 2x bandwidth for burst months
- Staged ramp credits: Month 1–3: 40% credit on overage tokens, Month 4–6: 25%, Month 7–12: 10%
- Multi-year option: 2-year commit converts to additional 8% term discount at renewal

I’ve copied Rachel to capture the technical SLOs and Marissa to confirm the concession schedule. Attached: Velox-Annual-Prepay-Proposal-v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB).

Next step: if this looks broadly acceptable, we can send a redline-friendly Word contract and a DocuSign envelope for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
——

From: Susan Park <susan.park@velox.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@velox.ai>, procurement@velox.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot results + proposal to move to annual prepay

Karthik —

Thanks for the proposal and for pulling the staged credits together. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement:
1) Can the ramp credits be applied as dollar credits against the committed invoice or do they only offset overages?
2) If we hit a usage plateau below the commit in months 4–6, how do true-ups work?
3) Are the bandwidth burst allowances pooled across our teams or per-product?

Also, procurement prefers a single consolidated invoice for the annual prepay rather than multiple monthly invoices. Can Marissa confirm billing cadence options?

—Susan
VP Product, Velox AI

On Mon, Sep 28, 2026 at 10:05 AM, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@velox.ai> wrote:
> Quick add: we need a standard SOC2 data handling addendum with the contract. Procurement will expect evidence before signature.
> 

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Susan Park <susan.park@velox.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-29T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot results + proposal to move to annual prepay

Thanks — answering inline:

1) Credits: We can apply staged credits in two ways; (A) as dollar credits that reduce your annual invoice (preferred for accounting simplicity), or (B) as overage credits that only apply when usage exceeds the commit. For Velox I recommend (A) so you get predictable billing during ramp.

2) True-ups: If usage is consistently below the commit for three consecutive months after month 6, we’ll move to a quarterly true-up where unused commit can be converted to a discounted token bank valid for the remaining term. We do not auto-bill for underutilization.

3) Burst bandwidth: pooled across your organization in the account-level config; we’ll include an addendum that sets per-product soft limits.

Billing cadence options: annual prepaid invoice (single upfront payment), or quarterly invoiced prepay (split the commit into 4 invoices with the same commitment terms). Annual upfront gets an extra 2.5% administrative discount.

Attachments: Velox-Redline-Commitment-20261001.docx (Word, 45KB) attached for redline. SOC2 evidence: I’ve included a link to our compliance package in the DocuSign cover note.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-01T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot results + proposal to move to annual prepay

Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a one-page concession table embedded in the updated proposal (Velox-Annual-Prepay-Proposal-v3.pdf) and the redline doc (Velox-Redline-Commitment-20261001.docx). Summary here:

- Effective unit price per MM tokens:
  Months 0–3: $75 / MM (after 40% staged credit)
  Months 4–6: $90 / MM (after 25% staged credit)
  Months 7–12: $108 / MM (after 10% staged credit)

- Burst cap: we can cap any single product at 3x baseline for burst. Account-level pool remains 6x but we will include a per-product hard cap at 3x as requested.

- True-up language: if average monthly usage for three consecutive months falls below 60% of the committed monthly equivalent after the 6-month ramp, the parties will enter a quarterly review to convert a portion of unused commit to a token bank at a 30% discount to list for remainder of term. We included the exact clause in the Word redline.

We can prepare the DocuSign envelope once you confirm the preferred billing cadence (annual upfront vs quarterly prepay). If you choose annual upfront, Marissa noted there’s a 2.5% administrative discount.

Karthik
